Let me first say how much I do love your site. I have belonged to Knit-It-Now, Knitter's Edge, and tried Bente Ronberg's English website. I am sure you know that Knit-It-Now is the absolute best by far. I watch your live shows, watch every tip of the week, and visit the blog often.  I have already had a subscription to your site and do not plan on renewing my subscription because I know most of what is there. I do, however, have a curiosity about the few things you have added, and I have got some new (old) yarn since my subscription expired that I would like to maybe use for a couple of the dynamic patterns. However, I cannot justify spending another $100 for the few things I have mentioned.  I was wondering if you plan to allow for previous subscribers to subscribe for a few months instead of the whole year. I know I would spend the $35 you offer in your Three Payments plan for only 3-4 months worth of a subscription. Maybe there are others who would do this also. 2-23 former dealer in her 80's she shared her story  At age 24 when visiting a friend she showed me a small basic knitting machine.  She threaded it up and we knit a simple scarf in a small amount of time.  I was hooked.  I had been a hand knitter for several years by then.  McCalls Needlecraft magazine advertised a brand of knitting machines, but I couldn’t afford it at time.  When my husband got a promotion and we moved to Lansing, Michigan I got a job and started working full time as the kids were in junior high and in high school.     So I saved my  money and summer of 1976 at age 39 bought my first knitting machine from Joan Ebach, Ada, Michigan a Brother dealer……a Brother punchcard  standard knitting machine.  Joan Ebach had her shop in her home so she invited me to come after lunch, stay over night, and we knitted through suppertime and were up early, had breakfast and knitted through mid afternoon, then I drove the 60 miles  home.   Another 3 months later I went back and bought  the ribber attachment.  She gave me the name of Ken and Marge (wholesalers) and I started mentioning to my friends I had the knitting machine and could sell and teach.  So on Saturdays I did.  Ladies and I sat in family room and they learned to knit and husbands sat in living room and watched ball games on my TV;  That way they were not picking on their wife while she took her lesson.     My husband died in 1980 so I moved to a condo. When I married my second husband 3 years later, he encouraged me to get into an actual shop situation as he could support our family on his salary.     The Skein Haus was a hand knitting store who also carried needlepoint and counted cross stitch, invited me to lease some of their space  and run my Shop, Eleanor Knitting Machines, from there.  By then I carried Brother machines and Passap machines.  Loved it even though hours were long. Never felt it was work.  Loved meeting the people.  Several are still my friends. Seven years later they sold the Skein Haus and the new owner did not want me there.  As it worked out Brother quit making their machines a couple of years later and Passap quit one year later.  I still serviced my current customers with yarn and when my husband and I retired from our regular jobs, we traveled a bit.  Still have a Brother 970 electronic and a Brother bulky machine.  Bought a Tiatexma midguage before you started carrying them.  Love my machines.
